title: 2 Samuel Chapter 17 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 17 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 17 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 17.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 17, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Ahithophel giving counsel
Hushai being called
Absalom speaking to Hushai
David being pursued
questions.correctAnswer: Ahithophel giving counsel
questions.explanation: Ahithophel is the first mentioned in the chapter as he gives counsel to Absalom in 2 Samuel 17:1.

questions.question: What did Ahithophel suggest he would do in his counsel to Absalom?
options: Pursue David with twelve thousand men
Hide from David
Gather more elders
Call for a meeting
questions.correctAnswer: Pursue David with twelve thousand men
questions.explanation: Ahithophel suggested he would pursue David with twelve thousand men in 2 Samuel 17:1.

questions.question: According to Ahithophel, what was David's condition when he pursued him?
options: Strong and powerful
Weary and weak handed
Hiding in a cave
With a large army
questions.correctAnswer: Weary and weak handed
questions.explanation: Ahithophel described David as weary and weak handed in 2 Samuel 17:2.

questions.question: What did Ahithophel promise to bring back to Absalom?
options: All the people
David's head
A message from David
A treaty with Israel
questions.correctAnswer: All the people
questions.explanation: Ahithophel promised to bring back all the people to Absalom in 2 Samuel 17:3.

questions.question: How did Absalom react to Ahithophel's counsel?
options: He was angry
He was pleased
He ignored it
He called for a vote
questions.correctAnswer: He was pleased
questions.explanation: Absalom was pleased with Ahithophel's counsel in 2 Samuel 17:4.

questions.question: Who did Absalom call after hearing Ahithophel's counsel?
options: Hushai the Archite
David
The elders of Israel
Joab
questions.correctAnswer: Hushai the Archite
questions.explanation: Absalom called for Hushai the Archite to hear his opinion after Ahithophel's counsel in 2 Samuel 17:5.

questions.question: What did Hushai think of Ahithophel's counsel?
options: It was wise
It was not good
It was necessary
It was too late
questions.correctAnswer: It was not good
questions.explanation: Hushai stated that the counsel of Ahithophel was not good at that time in 2 Samuel 17:7.

questions.question: How did Hushai describe David and his men?
options: Weak and fearful
Mighty men
Cowards
Disorganized
questions.correctAnswer: Mighty men
questions.explanation: Hushai described David and his men as mighty men in 2 Samuel 17:8.

questions.question: What did Hushai compare David's men to?
options: Lions
Bears robbed of whelps
Eagles
Wolves
questions.correctAnswer: Bears robbed of whelps
questions.explanation: Hushai compared David's men to bears robbed of their whelps in 2 Samuel 17:8.

questions.question: What did Hushai predict would happen if David's men were overthrown?
options: They would flee
There would be a slaughter
They would regroup
They would seek peace
questions.correctAnswer: There would be a slaughter
questions.explanation: Hushai predicted that if David's men were overthrown, there would be a slaughter among the people following Absalom in 2 Samuel 17:9.

questions.question: How did Hushai describe the heart of a valiant man?
options: As brave as a lion
As weak as a mouse
As calm as a dove
As quick as a rabbit
questions.correctAnswer: As brave as a lion
questions.explanation: Hushai described the heart of a valiant man as being as the heart of a lion in 2 Samuel 17:10.

questions.question: True or False: Ahithophel proposed to pursue David at night.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ahithophel proposed to pursue David during the night in 2 Samuel 17:1.

questions.question: True or False: Hushai agreed with Ahithophel's counsel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hushai disagreed with Ahithophel's counsel, stating it was not good at that time in 2 Samuel 17:7.

questions.question: True or False: Absalom was unhappy with the advice given by Hushai.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not indicate that Absalom was unhappy with Hushai's advice; rather, it was Ahithophel's counsel that he initially pleased Absalom in 2 Samuel 17:4.

questions.question: True or False: Hushai claimed that David was with a large army.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hushai did not claim that David was with a large army; instead, he indicated that David's men were mighty but did not specify their numbers in 2 Samuel 17:8.

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 17 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 17 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 17:11, what did Ahithophel counsel Absalom to do before going to battle?
options: Gather all Israel from Dan to Beersheba as the sand by the sea and go to battle in person
Wait for David to make the first move
Send spies to infiltrate David's camp
Build a strong fortress in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: Gather all Israel from Dan to Beersheba as the sand by the sea and go to battle in person
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:11 clearly states Ahithophel's counsel to gather all Israel from Dan to Beersheba, as numerous as the sand by the sea, and that Absalom should go to battle in his own person.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 17:12 promise will happen if Absalom goes to battle in person as 2 Samuel 17:11 commands?
options: They will find David and leave not one man with him
David will escape and regroup
The battle will be prolonged for many days
Only a few of David's men will be defeated
questions.correctAnswer: They will find David and leave not one man with him
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:12 promises that if Absalom goes to battle as advised, they will find David wherever he is and strike him down along with all his men, leaving not one.

questions.question: What extreme measure did Ahithophel advise if David escaped into a city, according to 2 Samuel 17:13?
options: Bring ropes to draw the city into the river until no stone remains
Lay siege to the city until David surrenders
Surround the city and starve them out
Set fire to the city gates
questions.correctAnswer: Bring ropes to draw the city into the river until no stone remains
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:13 describes Ahithophel's counsel that if David took refuge in a city, all Israel should bring ropes to that city and draw it into the river until not one small stone is left.

questions.question: How did the LORD intervene in the counsel between Ahithophel and Hushai as stated in 2 Samuel 17:14 and 2 Samuel 17:7?
options: The LORD appointed to defeat Ahithophel's good counsel to bring evil on Absalom
The LORD strengthened Ahithophel's counsel to ensure Absalom's victory
The LORD remained neutral in their counsel
The LORD confused Hushai's counsel to mislead Absalom
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD appointed to defeat Ahithophel's good counsel to bring evil on Absalom
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:14 states the LORD had appointed to defeat Ahithophel's good counsel in order to bring evil upon Absalom, aligning with 2 Samuel 17:7 where Hushai advises against Ahithophel's counsel.

questions.question: What practical advice did Hushai give to Absalom about David's state and behavior in 2 Samuel 17:8?
options: David is a man of war, mighty and valiant, and will not lodge with the people
David is weak and fearful, likely to flee quickly
David is hiding and cannot be found
David's men are disorganized and disheartened
questions.correctAnswer: David is a man of war, mighty and valiant, and will not lodge with the people
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:8 explains that David is a mighty man of war and valiant, who will not lodge with the people, indicating he is prepared and dangerous.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 17:16, what was the urgent message Hushai instructed Zadok and Abiathar to send to David?
options: Do not lodge in the plains of the wilderness, pass over quickly to avoid being swallowed up
Prepare for battle at once in the wilderness
Hide in the city of Jerusalem until reinforcements arrive
Send out spies to learn Absalom’s plans
questions.correctAnswer: Do not lodge in the plains of the wilderness, pass over quickly to avoid being swallowed up
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:16 records Hushai's urgent message to David not to lodge in the plains of the wilderness but to pass over quickly lest the king and his people be swallowed up.

questions.question: What was the method used by the woman in Bahurim to hide Jonathan and Ahimaaz from Absalom's servants as described in 2 Samuel 17:19?
options: She spread a covering over the well's mouth and ground corn on it
She hid them in a secret room
She sent them away disguised as merchants
She told the servants they had fled the city
questions.correctAnswer: She spread a covering over the well's mouth and ground corn on it
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:19 describes the woman’s clever tactic of covering the well’s mouth with a covering and spreading ground corn on it so that the hiding place was not discovered.

questions.question: Why did Jonathan and Ahimaaz stay by Enrogel instead of entering the city, according to 2 Samuel 17:17?
options: Because they might not be seen entering the city
Because they were waiting for reinforcements
Because they were injured
Because they were guarding the city gates
questions.correctAnswer: Because they might not be seen entering the city
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:17 states Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed by Enrogel because they might not be seen coming into the city, indicating a need for secrecy.

questions.question: What was the overall result of Hushai’s counsel compared to Ahithophel’s, as expressed in 2 Samuel 17:14?
options: Absalom and the elders said Hushai’s counsel was better than Ahithophel’s
Absalom ignored both counsels and acted on his own
Absalom chose to follow Ahithophel’s counsel only
Absalom was confused and delayed his decision
questions.correctAnswer: Absalom and the elders said Hushai’s counsel was better than Ahithophel’s
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:14 records that Absalom and all the men of Israel said the counsel of Hushai was better than that of Ahithophel, in line with the LORD’s plan.

questions.question: In light of 2 Samuel 17:10, how would the initial defeat of some of David's men affect the morale of others?
options: Those who hear of the defeat will melt in fear, believing a slaughter occurred
They will be encouraged to fight harder
They will immediately seek peace negotiations
They will be indifferent to the news
questions.correctAnswer: Those who hear of the defeat will melt in fear, believing a slaughter occurred
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:9-10 explain that if some of David's men are overthrown, others will hear and say a slaughter has happened, causing even valiant men to melt away in fear.

questions.question: What does the story of the woman hiding Jonathan and Ahimaaz teach about practical faith and integrity under pressure?
options: Courage and cleverness in protecting God's servants can preserve His plans
Avoiding risk is the best way to serve God
Deception is never allowed, even for righteous causes
One should always flee rather than hide
questions.correctAnswer: Courage and cleverness in protecting God's servants can preserve His plans
questions.explanation: The woman’s actions in 2 Samuel 17:18-20 show practical faith and integrity, courageously protecting the king’s messengers and thus helping preserve God’s plan.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 17:15 show Hushai’s role in the conflict between Absalom and David?
options: Hushai reports Ahithophel's counsel and his own opposing counsel to the priests to send a warning to David
Hushai abandons Absalom and joins David openly
Hushai refuses to speak to priests or elders
Hushai advises Absalom to attack immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Hushai reports Ahithophel's counsel and his own opposing counsel to the priests to send a warning to David
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:15 shows Hushai explaining Ahithophel’s counsel and his own opposing counsel to Zadok and Abiathar so they can relay a warning to David.

questions.question: What practical spiritual lesson can be drawn from the LORD appointing to defeat Ahithophel’s counsel as in 2 Samuel 17:14?
options: God can use even evil counsel to fulfill His righteous purposes by overriding human plans
Human wisdom is always superior to divine intervention
God does not intervene in human conflicts
All counsel is equally good in God’s eyes
questions.correctAnswer: God can use even evil counsel to fulfill His righteous purposes by overriding human plans
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:14 reveals that the LORD appointed to defeat Ahithophel’s counsel to bring evil on Absalom, showing God's sovereignty over human schemes.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Samuel 17:19, the woman’s covering of the well’s mouth was so effective that Absalom’s servants did not discover Jonathan and Ahimaaz.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:19 states that the woman spread a covering over the well’s mouth along with ground corn, and the hiding was not known by Absalom’s servants.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Samuel 17:16, Hushai advised David to stay and fortify in the plains of the wilderness to prepare for battle.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:16 instructs David not to lodge in the plains of the wilderness but to pass over quickly to avoid being swallowed up, so staying to fortify is contrary to this advice.

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 17 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 17.

questions.question: After Ahithophel's counsel was not followed, what action did he take according to 2 Samuel 17:23?
options: He saddled his ass, went home, put his household in order, and hanged himself
He fled to another country
He sought forgiveness from David
He joined Absalom's army
questions.correctAnswer: He saddled his ass, went home, put his household in order, and hanged himself
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:23 explains that Ahithophel saddled his ass, went home, put his household in order, and then hanged himself, leading to his death.

questions.question: What instruction did Ahimaaz and Jonathan give to King David after coming out of the well according to 2 Samuel 17:21?
options: Arise, and pass quickly over the water
Stay hidden in the wilderness
Prepare for battle immediately
Send messengers to Absalom
questions.correctAnswer: Arise, and pass quickly over the water
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 17:21, Ahimaaz and Jonathan told David to arise and pass quickly over the water because Ahithophel had counseled against him.

questions.question: Where did David and his people pass over according to 2 Samuel 17:22?
options: Jordan
Euphrates
Nile
Tigris
questions.correctAnswer: Jordan
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:22 states explicitly that David and all the people with him passed over the Jordan river by morning light.

questions.question: Who did Absalom appoint as captain of the host instead of Joab according to 2 Samuel 17:25?
options: Amasa
Ithra
Machir
Shobi
questions.correctAnswer: Amasa
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:25 records that Absalom made Amasa captain of the host instead of Joab.

questions.question: What items did Shobi, Machir, and Barzillai bring to David and his people at Mahanaim according to 2 Samuel 17:28?
options: Beds, basons, earthen vessels, wheat, barley, flour, parched corn, beans, lentiles, parched pulse
Gold, silver, weapons and armor
Cattle, sheep, and goats
Fruits, vegetables, and wine
questions.correctAnswer: Beds, basons, earthen vessels, wheat, barley, flour, parched corn, beans, lentiles, parched pulse
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:28 explicitly lists these items as those brought for David and his people, emphasizing their need for sustenance.

questions.question: Why did Shobi, Machir, and Barzillai bring food and supplies to David according to 2 Samuel 17:29?
options: Because the people were hungry, weary, and thirsty in the wilderness
To bribe David for political favor
To prepare David for a feast
To celebrate Absalom's reign
questions.correctAnswer: Because the people were hungry, weary, and thirsty in the wilderness
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:29 states that these provisions were brought because the people with David were hungry, weary, and thirsty in the wilderness.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'chafed' (used in 2 Samuel 17:8) most closely mean?
options: Angry or roused to fury
Tired or weary
Confused or perplexed
Joyful and hopeful
questions.correctAnswer: Angry or roused to fury
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 17:8, the Hebrew word translated as 'chafed' describes David's men being angry or fiercely protective, like a bear robbed of her whelps.

questions.question: Which literary device is exemplified in Hushai's counsel contrasting Ahithophel's advice in 2 Samuel 17:7-14?
options: Chiasmus
Alliteration
Parallelism
Metaphor
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: The passage shows a chiastic structure where the two opposing counsels (Ahithophel’s and Hushai’s) are contrasted in a symmetrical pattern, highlighting the reversal of fortune.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of rejected counsel and divine sovereignty found in 2 Samuel 17:14?
options: Acts 2:23
Romans 8:28
Revelation 13:7
Hebrews 11:32
questions.correctAnswer: Acts 2:23
questions.explanation: Acts 2:23 echoes the theme of God's sovereign plan working through human counsel and rejection, as God appointed to defeat Ahithophel's counsel in 2 Samuel 17:14.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects with the theme of fleeing and crossing a river for safety, similar to David's crossing in 2 Samuel 17:22?
options: Exodus 14:21-22
Genesis 6:17
Joshua 3:14-17
Judges 7:5
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 14:21-22
questions.explanation: Exodus 14:21-22 describes the Israelites crossing the Red Sea to escape Pharaoh, paralleling David's crossing of the Jordan in 2 Samuel 17:22 for safety.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the instructions given by Ahimaaz and Jonathan in 2 Samuel 17:21?
options: Their hiding in a well covered with a spreading of corn
The battle between David's and Absalom's forces
The sending of Hushai to Absalom
Absalom appointing Amasa as captain
questions.correctAnswer: Their hiding in a well covered with a spreading of corn
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:18-20 describes Ahimaaz and Jonathan hiding in a well covered with corn before they came up and delivered the message in verse 21.

questions.question: What typological significance does Ahithophel's suicide in 2 Samuel 17:23 hold in biblical literature?
options: It foreshadows Judas Iscariot’s betrayal and suicide
It symbolizes the fall of a false prophet
It represents the end of the Davidic covenant
It indicates divine judgment on idolatry
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Judas Iscariot’s betrayal and suicide
questions.explanation: Ahithophel’s suicide after his counsel is rejected is often seen as a typological foreshadowing of Judas Iscariot’s betrayal and subsequent suicide in the New Testament.

questions.question: How does the mention of 'beds, basons, and earthen vessels' in 2 Samuel 17:28 reflect the cultural and historical context of hospitality in ancient Israel?
options: They represent provisions for both comfort and sustenance in a nomadic setting
They are symbolic offerings to the temple
They indicate preparations for a royal coronation
They are ritual objects for sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: They represent provisions for both comfort and sustenance in a nomadic setting
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:28 lists these items as necessary for hospitality, reflecting the practical needs of comfort and food in the wilderness context where David stayed.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Samuel 17:22, not one person was left behind when David and his people crossed the Jordan.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:22 states that by morning light, there lacked not one of them that was not gone over Jordan, confirming all crossed.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Samuel 17:25, Amasa was the son of Joab.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:25 clarifies that Amasa was the son of Ithra, an Israelite, not Joab.

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 17 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 17 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Samuel 17:14 teach about God's providence in relation to human counsel?
options: God sovereignly overrules human plans for His purposes
Human counsel is always superior to divine will
God is unaware of human plotting
God passively permits all evil without intervention
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly overrules human plans for His purposes
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 17:14 states that the LORD had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel to bring evil upon Absalom, showing God's sovereign control over human intentions.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment and human sin is taught in 2 Samuel 17:23 regarding Ahithophel?
options: Sin leads to despair and self-destruction
God immediately forgives all sins without consequence
Human plans are infallible and always succeed
Suicide is commended as a righteous act
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to despair and self-destruction
questions.explanation: Verse 23 records Ahithophel hanging himself after his counsel is rejected, illustrating the destructive consequences of sin and despair.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning God's protection and salvation is evident in 2 Samuel 17:22?
options: God preserves His people intact despite adversity
Salvation is earned by human strength alone
God abandons those who flee from conflict
Only a portion of God's people are saved
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves His people intact despite adversity
questions.explanation: Verse 22 emphasizes that not one of David's followers was lost crossing the Jordan, showing divine preservation amidst danger.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Samuel 17:14 specifically demonstrate?
options: Sovereignty
Immutability
Omnipresence
Justice
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: The LORD's appointment to defeat Ahithophel's counsel in verse 14 reveals God's sovereign control over events.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted by God's preservation of David's followers in 2 Samuel 17:22?
options: Providence
Wrath
Holiness
Foreknowledge
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: God's providential care is shown in the safe passage of David and his people as recorded in verse 22.

questions.question: How does the counsel conflict in 2 Samuel 17 prepare for the New Testament theme of spiritual warfare?
options: It illustrates the battle between good and evil influences on leadership
It teaches that all warfare is physical only
It denies the existence of spiritual opposition
It focuses solely on political intrigue without spiritual dimension
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the battle between good and evil influences on leadership
questions.explanation: The opposing counsels of Ahithophel and Hushai in this chapter foreshadow spiritual forces influencing human decisions, a theme expanded in the New Testament.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does 2 Samuel 17:23 have with the theme of divine judgment in Scripture?
options: It exemplifies the consequences of rejecting God's will
It shows that all sinners are spared
It promotes despair as a godly response
It denies any link between sin and judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies the consequences of rejecting God's will
questions.explanation: Ahithophel's suicide after his counsel is rejected reflects divine judgment on rebellion, aligning with biblical themes of judgment for sin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Samuel 17:14 and 2 Samuel 17:22 teach about God's providence and human responsibility?
options: God sovereignly directs outcomes while humans must act obediently
Human actions alone determine outcomes without divine influence
God's providence removes all human responsibility
Human plans always prevail over God's will
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly directs outcomes while humans must act obediently
questions.explanation: Verse 14 shows God's sovereign overruling of counsel, and verse 22 shows David's obedience in fleeing, together teaching divine sovereignty and human responsibility.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Samuel 17:23 and 2 Samuel 17:1 teach about sin, despair, and the consequences of rebellion?
options: Sinful counsel leads to despair and ultimate destruction
Rebellion always succeeds without consequence
Despair is unrelated to sin
God encourages rebellion through despair
questions.correctAnswer: Sinful counsel leads to despair and ultimate destruction
questions.explanation: Ahithophel's counsel (verse 1) and his subsequent suicide (verse 23) demonstrate how sinful rebellion leads to ruin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Samuel 17:8 and 2 Samuel 17:10 teach about the character of God’s anointed and the fear they inspire?
options: God’s anointed are mighty warriors who instill fear in their enemies
God’s anointed are weak and easily defeated
Might and fear in leaders come only from human strength
God’s anointed avoid conflict and flee
questions.correctAnswer: God’s anointed are mighty warriors who instill fear in their enemies
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 10 describe David as a mighty man of war whose presence causes fear, reflecting God's empowerment of His anointed.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 2 Samuel 17:14 implies God manipulates human free will unjustly. What does 2 Samuel 17:14 actually teach?
options: God uses His sovereign will to accomplish His righteous purposes without violating human responsibility
God forces people to act against their will arbitrarily
Human free will is an illusion with no real choices
God is unaware of human plans and does not intervene
questions.correctAnswer: God uses His sovereign will to accomplish His righteous purposes without violating human responsibility
questions.explanation: Verse 14 shows God appointing to defeat counsel for a greater purpose, consistent with biblical teaching on God's sovereignty and human responsibility.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Samuel 17:16 teach about divine guidance and human obedience in times of crisis?
options: God provides timely warnings through human agents which must be heeded
God leaves His people without guidance in trouble
Human obedience is irrelevant to divine protection
Warnings from humans are always unreliable
questions.correctAnswer: God provides timely warnings through human agents which must be heeded
questions.explanation: Verse 16 shows Hushai instructing the priests to warn David, emphasizing divine guidance through intermediaries and the need for obedience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by God's provision of food and supplies to David in 2 Samuel 17:27-29?
options: Faithfulness
Wrath
Jealousy
Immutability
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: Verses 27-29 show God's faithful provision for David and his weary followers through supporters, illustrating God’s sustaining faithfulness.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about human alliances and God's providence is taught in 2 Samuel 17:27-29?
options: God can use even foreign allies to sustain His people
God only works through Israel and never uses outsiders
Human alliances guarantee success without God's involvement
Provision comes solely from one's own efforts
questions.correctAnswer: God can use even foreign allies to sustain His people
questions.explanation: The passage mentions allies from Ammon and others providing for David, showing God’s providential use of diverse peoples.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 17:7-13 illustrate the theological principle of wisdom versus folly in leadership?
options: Hushai's counsel, though human, reflects prudence and understanding of God's people better than Ahithophel's rash plan
Ahithophel's counsel is wiser because it is swift and decisive
Leadership wisdom is irrelevant to outcomes
Folly always triumphs in political decisions
questions.correctAnswer: Hushai's counsel, though human, reflects prudence and understanding of God's people better than Ahithophel's rash plan
questions.explanation: Verses 7-13 show Hushai offering a more cautious and people-aware strategy, highlighting the value of wise counsel in line with divine purposes.
